#### What this PR does / why we need it:

xref: #127793

This PR fixes the pod with restartable init containers to have a proper phase after the pod sandbox re-creation.

Currently, the `runtime.PodStatus` cannot retrieve the active container statuses, which are the container statuses associated with the current pod sandbox. This adds the `ActiveContainerStatuses` to `runtime.PodStatus`, allowing it to include the container statuses of the current pod sandbox, and fixes the kubelet to correctly set the pod Phase to `Pending` when no active regular containers are present.

issue_context.title: [SidecarContainers] Failed to get proper phase after the node reboot
issue_context.body:
### What happened?

If a pod has an init container with restartPolicy "Always" (sidecar), it may lose the pending phase after the node reboot and start the regular containers before initializing the init containers.

/sig node
/priority important-soon
/kind bug

This is similar to https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/126650, but separated as it only affects the pod with restartable init containers.

### What did you expect to happen?

After the node reboot, the remaining pod should start from the pending phase and run the init containers one by one to initialize.

### How can we reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)?

1. Create and initialize the pod with an init container with "Always" container restart policy.
2. Restart the node.

### Anything else we need to know?

I am struggling with figuring out whether the current pod (sandbox) has initialized just by looking its container statuses.

One idea is to use `Initialized` condition along with `PodReadyToStartContainers` condition as `PodReadyToStartContainers` condition is re-set after the node reboots and the second pod sandbox is recreated.

cc @kannon92
I believe that is the intent of PodReadyToStartContainers.

> One idea is to use `Initialized` condition along with `PodReadyToStartContainers` condition as `PodReadyToStartContainers` condition is re-set after the node reboots and the second pod sandbox is recreated.

Since this approach doesn't reliably handle all cases, I'll try adding podSandboxID to `pkg/kubelet/container.Status` to identify whether the container status belongs to the current pod sandbox.
